# Incident Report — Network Traffic Analysis (MTA 2024-09-04)

## Evidence Reviewed
- `2024-09-04-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (5,091 frames, ~59 min capture)
- `2024-09-04-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.txt` (Suricata/ET alert export)
- `2024-09-04-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.jpg` (alert screenshot, consistent with .txt)

Analysis performed with `tshark` (protocol hierarchy, DHCP/NBNS/Kerberos field extraction, HTTP request/object export, TCP stream follow, IP conversation stats).

## 1. Infected Host
| Attribute | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **172.17.0.99** | consistent across DHCP, ARP, NBNS, HTTP, Kerberos |
| MAC address | **18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4** | DHCP Discover/Request, ARP replies |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** | DHCP option 12, NBNS name registration, DNS PTR/A queries |
| Logged-in domain user | **afletcher** (domain `BEPOSITIVE`/`bepositive.com`) | Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString `afletcher`, realm `BEPOSITIVE.COM`, exchanged with DC 172.17.0.17 (`WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19.bepositive.com`) |
| OS | Windows 10 (WOW64) | User-Agent strings on all outbound HTTP: `Windows NT 10.0; WOW64; Trident/7.0` |

The host is a domain-joined Windows 10 workstation on the `bepositive.com` AD domain, DC at 172.17.0.17.

## 2. Malware Family
**Koi Stealer** (Win32/Koi Stealer).

- **Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The alert log contains a direct hit: `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` (Event #3.1504, 48 occurrences), fired against 172.17.0.99 → 79.124.78.197:80.
- **Corroborating behavioral evidence** observed directly in the pcap:
  - Repeated `POST /foots.php` to 79.124.78.197 with `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`, `Content-Encoding: binary`, opaque encrypted body (no readable content) — classic stealer exfil/heartbeat channel.
  - A `GET /index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` returned a plaintext bot-registration token: `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|` — bot ID / affiliate (subid) / C2-URL triplet typical of stealer/loader check-in protocols.
  - Beacon cadence: initial check-ins carry 94/112/40-byte bodies, then settle into a steady ~60–70 second heartbeat of 40-byte encrypted POSTs, continuing for the remainder of the capture (96 total `/foots.php` requests observed).
  - All malicious requests share the same fixed/spoofed User-Agent: `Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; WOW64; Trident/7.0; .NET4.0C; .NET4.0E; .NET CLR 2.0.50727; .NET CLR 3.0.30729; .NET CLR 3.5.30729)`.

Also flagged in the alert log (Event #3.1497, 50 hits): `ET INFO GENERIC SUSPICIOUS POST to Dotted Quad with Fake Browser` — same host/port, confirming the "POST to a raw IP with a spoofed old-IE UA" pattern.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control endpoint**
- `79.124.78.197:80` (HTTP, `Server: nginx`) — Koi Stealer C2. No DNS lookup precedes this connection; the malware connects directly to the IP, bypassing DNS.

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` — beacon/exfil POST endpoint (96 requests over the session)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` — bot check-in/registration (POST)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` — GET returning bot ID/config: `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|`

**Suspected staging/delivery site**
- `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` resolving to `46.254.34.201:443` (TLS). This connection begins at t=153.3s in the capture, and the first C2 beacon to 79.124.78.197 begins only 2.1 seconds later at t=155.4s, with the two hosts alternating again shortly after (t=157.9s / t=159.6s). This timing strongly suggests it is the delivery/staging channel, but the session is TLS-encrypted end to end — no plaintext file transfer, filename, or hash could be recovered from it. Flagging as a probable but **not traffic-confirmed** delivery vector.

**Malicious domains**
- No malware-related domain was resolved via DNS in this capture — the C2 channel is IP-direct (79.124.78.197), and the only external domain tied to the intrusion timeline is `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (46.254.34.201), used over TLS.

**Transferred files / hashes**
- **None observed.** No executable, script, or document object was transferred in the clear over HTTP in this capture. All C2 traffic to 79.124.78.197 uses `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` / `Content-Encoding: binary` opaque bodies, and the suspected staging connection to 46.254.34.201 is fully TLS-encrypted. No SHA256 can be honestly derived from this evidence — do not treat any hash as present unless it is later obtained from host-based/EDR artifacts.

**Alert-log entries not tied to the compromise (noted for completeness, assessed as benign/false-positive)**
- `ET POLICY Reserved Internal IP Traffic`, `ET DNS Standard query response Name Error`, `ET INFO Terse Request for .txt`/`Microsoft Connection Test` (both against Akamai IPs 23.220.251.149/.158 hosting `www.msftconnecttest.com` — legitimate Windows NCSI checks)
- `ET INFO Potentially unsafe SMBv1`, `GPL NETBIOS SMB Session Setup NTMLSSP unicode asn1 overflow attempt`, `GPL NETBIOS SMB IPC$ unicode share access`, `GPL NETBIOS SMB_COM_TRANSACTION Max Data Count of 0 DOS Attempt`, `GPL RPC kerberos principal name overflow TCP` — all against the domain controller 172.17.0.17 on ports 139/88, consistent with normal domain-joined SMB/Kerberos authentication traffic between DESKTOP-RNVO9AT and its DC, not exploitation.

## Summary
DESKTOP-RNVO9AT (172.17.0.99, MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4), logged in as domain user `afletcher` on `bepositive.com`, is compromised with **Koi Stealer** (ETPRO signature-confirmed). The malware beacons every ~60–70 seconds to C2 **79.124.78.197:80** via `/foots.php` (heartbeat/exfil) and `/index.php` (bot registration, bot ID `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn`, affiliate/subid `qIOuKk7U`). A TLS session to `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (46.254.34.201) immediately precedes the first C2 beacon and is the likely delivery/staging vector, though encryption prevented recovery of any dropped file or hash from this capture.
